item.title: The Politics of Inclusion and Exclusion in Smart Cities
item.content:encoded:
This special issue examines the political dimensions of smart city development, focusing on how technological implementations shape patterns of inclusion and exclusion within urban environments. The call invites research that critically analyzes the social and political consequences of smart city initiatives.

Appel publié par Cities. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Timeline

  • June 30, 2027: Submission deadline

item.title: Urban Tourism Intelligence and Behavioral Innovation for Smart and Sustainable City Centers
item.content:encoded:
Hew Soon-Hin, Multimedia University

Nigel Morgan, Manchester Metropolitan University

Giuseppe Piero-Guido, University of Calabria

Aleksandra Vujko, Singidunum University

This special issue examines how smart technologies, behavioral sciences, and data-driven systems are transforming urban tourism to create sustainable and intelligent city centers. It focuses on the intersection of AI-powered tourism analytics, IoT-enabled mobility, digital engagement, and policy frameworks that enhance visitor experiences while maintaining environmental resilience and cultural integrity.

Appel publié par International Journal of Tourism Cities. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Smart-sensor enabled visitor behaviour analytics for resilient city centre tourism ecosystems
  • Behavioural nudging via augmented reality to foster sustainable urban tourism practices
  • Data-driven co-creation of urban tourism experiences engaging local residents and visitors
  • Mobility platform integration and behavioural adaptation in smart tourism city hubs
  • Gamification of eco-tourism behaviour in urban destinations employing IoT technologies
  • Personalised micro-itineraries and behavioural segmentation for smart sustainable city tourism
  • Digital twin modelling of tourist flows and behavioural responses in city centres
  • Ethics, trust and behavioural change in AI-mediated urban tourism services
  • Smart governance frameworks enabling behavioural innovation for inclusive urban tourism
  • Wearable technologies and tourist behaviour monitoring to optimise smart city tourism
  • Blockchain-enabled incentives for sustainable visitor behaviours in urban tourism environments

Timeline

  • April 10, 2026: Abstract deadline
  • September 20, 2026: Manuscript deadline
